cards.text: The Lord GOD is speaking to Ezekiel, His prophet, and He calls him "son of man." In the last chapter, God said Gog of the land of Magog would come out of the far north against His people Israel "like a cloud covering the land" (Ezekiel 38:2, 15-16). Now God tells Ezekiel to prophesy against Gog again, with the same words as before: "Behold, I am against you, O Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal."

God says He'll turn Gog around, drive him along, bring him up from the far north and send him against the mountains of Israel. I bet Gog thinks he's running this invasion, but friend, he's not even holding the wheel.

cards.question: Gog shows up with a bow in his left hand and arrows in his right. What does God say He'll do to them?

answers.text: Strike them out of his hands
Break them in front of him

cards.question: On the mountains of Israel, Gog falls, but his troops and the nations with him get away.

cards.text: Gog, his troops, the nations with him: they all fall. And God says He'll give them as food to every kind of ravenous bird and wild beast.

cards.question: God says Gog will fall in the open field. What reason does He give for being so sure?

cards.text: Then God goes past the battlefield. He says He'll send fire on Magog, Gog's own land, and on "those who dwell securely in the coastlands".

cards.question: After God sends fire on Magog and the coastlands, they will know that He is the LORD.
God will make His holy name known among His people Israel and will no longer allow it to be ___.

cards.text: God says, "Yes, it is coming, and it will surely happen," and He calls it the day He has spoken of. No maybe in that, friend.

Then the people in Israel's cities go out, kindle fires and burn up the weapons: bucklers and shields, bows and arrows, clubs and spears. Gog packed the whole armory, and Israel just brought the matches.

cards.question: Israel uses Gog's weapons for fuel for seven ___.

cards.text: SEVEN YEARS of fuel, and nobody gathers wood from the countryside or cuts it from the forests. Friend, I can't make it seven DAYS without running out of chocolate chips.

cards.question: In the end, Israel plunders those who plundered them.

cards.text: On that day, God gives Gog a burial place in Israel: the Valley of the Travelers, east of the Sea. Gog and all his hordes are buried there, and it blocks those who travel through.

cards.question: Because Gog and all his hordes are buried in the Valley of the Travelers, what does it end up being called?
For seven ___ the house of Israel buries Gog's hordes in order to ___ the land.

cards.text: All the people of the land join in, and God says it will bring them renown on the day He displays His glory. Then men are employed to keep passing through the land, burying any invaders still on the ground.

cards.question: During the search, anyone who sees a human bone sets something up next to it. What is it?

cards.text: That pillar stays until the gravediggers bury the bone in the Valley of Hamon-gog. Even a city gets the name Hamonah, and so they cleanse the land.
Then God tells Ezekiel to call out to every kind of bird and every beast of the field. I invite bakers one at a time, friend, and Ezekiel's inviting the whole sky.

cards.question: God tells the birds and beasts to gather from all around. What's He preparing for them on the mountains of Israel?

cards.text: The birds and beasts eat at what God calls His table. They feast on the mighty and the princes of the earth, with horses and riders and warriors of every kind.

cards.question: God says only Israel will see the judgment He executes.

cards.text: God says He'll display His glory among the nations. And from that day forward, the house of Israel will know that He is the LORD their God.

cards.question: The nations will also learn why the house of Israel went into exile. What was the reason?
Because Israel was unfaithful, God hid His face from them and delivered them into the hands of their enemies.

cards.text: God dealt with them according to their uncleanness and transgressions. And there's that line again: He hid His face from them.
Then comes a big "Therefore." God says He will have compassion on the whole house of Israel, and He will be jealous for His holy name.

cards.question: Now God speaks about Jacob, meaning His people Israel. What does He say He will do for them?
When Israel dwells securely in their land, they will ___ their disgrace.

cards.text: And they'll live with no one to frighten them. I spent years in a junk drawer jumping every time it rattled open, so friend, that's my DREAM right there.

cards.question: As God gathers Israel out of the lands of their enemies, He will show His ___ in them in the sight of many nations.
When God regathers Israel to their own land, He leaves a few of them behind among the nations.

cards.text: NOT ONE of them left behind, and then they will know that He is the LORD their God. Nobody gets stuck in the back of the drawer on this one, friend.

cards.question: God will no longer hide His face from them, for He will pour out His ___ on the house of Israel.

cards.text: From "I hid My face" to "I will pour out My Spirit." That's where God ends His whole message about Gog, friend: with a promise.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 quotes "son of man.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 17 quotes "I will pour out My Spirit.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2's choice cards open MC, TF, MC, TF (cards 2, 4, 6, 7). That matches stop 1's opening MC, TF, MC, TF (cards 3, 4, 6, 8). Within stop 1, cards 3 to 8 also simply alternate MC and TF.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the BSB word 'profaned', which no card has shown or set up. It follows a choice card with no story card for 39:7, so nothing says the name was being dishonored. The pick tests unseen wording, not reasoned meaning. 'changed' and 'replaced' only fall away because they sound odd.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: 'In the end' adds a time marker that Ezekiel 39:10 doesn't have. The verse simply says they will plunder those who plundered them.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: 'During the search' points back to a search no card has set up. Card 18 skips 39:14b ('At the end of the seven months they will begin their search'), so the question doesn't say who is searching or for what.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'No maybe in that, friend.' is a mild, pleasant tag, not a real laugh. The moment ('it will surely happen') could carry a stronger Papa Dorin reaction without muddying a fact.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Their iniquity against God' is a spiritual, Bible-worded noun phrase. Both wrong answers are military clauses ('Their army was too small', 'Their walls were too weak'). The right answer is a different kind of thing and sounds more like the Bible, so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The last card only looks back over 39:24-29 ('From "I hid My face" to "I will pour out My Spirit."'). It tells no new part of the passage, so it's a recap card.

Many cards narrate God's prophecy as events happening now, with no 'God says' framing. Examples: stop 1 card 11 ('Then the people in Israel's cities go out... Israel just brought the matches'), cards 14, 15, 17 and 20, and stop 2 card 3 ('The birds and beasts eat at what God calls His table'). In the text, all of this is God's future 'will' statements to Ezekiel. Stated as plain fact, it can read as narrated history or as Papa Dorin describing end-times events.
findings.question: In prophetic passages, can Papa Dorin retell God's future 'will' statements in the narrative present as events, or must each card keep them framed as what God says will happen?

findings.problem: The joke compares Papa Dorin inviting bakers (his invitation to prepare for the Marriage Supper) with Ezekiel summoning scavengers to a feast on fallen warriors. It doesn't target the Supper. But it ties his Supper invitations to a judgment feast of carrion, and the docs don't say whether that link is acceptable.
findings.question: Is it okay for a joke to compare Papa Dorin's invitations for the Marriage Supper to the scavengers' sacrificial feast of judgment in Ezekiel 39:17, or should the Supper-invitation image stay away from judgment-feast scenes?
